description: Seed data for the Bookly policy graph. Ingested by ingest.py into Neo4j, which is the only runtime policy store — nothing reads this file at runtime. Policy only: no customers, orders, items, or returns.

categories.name: PhysicalBook
categories.description: Printed books. Returnable, subject to a window.

categories.name: EBook
categories.description: Digital downloads. Not returnable once made available.

policies.name: Standard 30-day returns
policies.summary: Physical books may be returned within 30 days of delivery, in resalable condition.

policies.name: Digital purchases are final
policies.summary: Ebooks cannot be returned once the download has been made available.

policies.name: Holiday sale extended returns
policies.summary: Physical books bought during a Bookly holiday sale may be returned within 60 days of delivery instead of 30.

policies.name: Bookly Australia extended returns
policies.summary: A Bookly goodwill extension: customers in Australia get 45 days on physical books instead of 30. This is Bookly's own policy, not a statement about Australian law.

notes: Endpoints in `relationships` are natural keys: a category `name`, a policy `policy_id`, or a region `code`. AU is Australia.
DIGITAL_NO_RETURN has no window and nothing OVERRIDES it. The absence is the rule: no region or promotion can rescue an ebook, and DAMAGED_ON_ARRIVAL is not listed among its exceptions.
Precedence is stored twice on purpose: as a `precedence` property (cheap sort) and as OVERRIDES edges (explainable path). The edges are the source of truth for what gets explained to a customer.
